Plot Empirical Influence Values

Source: R/influence_plot.R
influence_plot.Rd

Creates a plot of empirical influence values for each case. The plot can optionally mark cases with the largest absolute influence.

Usage

influence_plot(
  object,
  column = NULL,
  plot_title = "Influence Plot",
  x_label = NULL,
  cutoff_x_low = NULL,
  cutoff_x_high = NULL,
  largest_x = NULL,
  absolute = FALSE,
  point_aes = list(),
  vline_aes = list(),
  hline_aes = list(),
  cutoff_line_aes = list(),
  case_label_aes = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

object

An object of class "influenceDiagnostic" returned by influence_diagnostic() or an "empiricalInfluence" vector returned by calculate_empirical_influence(), matrix, or data frame containing one or more numeric columns.

column

If object is a matrix or data frame, the column to plot.

plot_title

Title of the plot.

x_label

Label for the y-axis.

cutoff_x_low

Optional lower threshold for highlighting cases.

cutoff_x_high

Optional upper threshold for highlighting cases.

largest_x

Number of cases with largest absolute values to label.

absolute

Logical, whether to plot absolute influence values.

point_aes

Additional arguments passed to ggplot2::geom_point().

vline_aes

Additional arguments passed to ggplot2::geom_segment().

hline_aes

Additional arguments passed to ggplot2::geom_hline().

cutoff_line_aes

Additional arguments passed to ggplot2::geom_hline() for cutoff lines.

case_label_aes

Additional arguments passed to ggrepel::geom_label_repel().

...

Additional arguments (currently unused).

Value

A ggplot object.
